notes:
Summary: Lodestar DataWorks (EU-based insurtech) evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) to replace a fragile internal inference stack. Strong emphasis on data residency (EU), customer-managed KMS/HSM, and auditable logs forwarded to Splunk. Wants Terraform + Helm POC inside their AWS account.

Conversation snippets / call notes:
- 'We cannot have any token data leave our VPC; audit trail must be complete.' (Head of Sec)
- Customer prefers AWS KMS with cross-account key policy and optional HSM-backed key.
- Latency: target p95 chat < 200ms for 1-2k concurrent users in peak; throughput target ~50 rps for embeddings pipeline.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to pay premium for isolation but wants clear unit cost numbers; demo must include Redwood Optimize recommendations.

POC ask / scope (customer requested):
- Deploy Redwood Private control plane connector and inference nodes into customer-managed VPC using our Terraform module and Helm charts (they will run in their AWS account).
- KMS: show KMS integration with envelope encryption, demo cross-account IAM roles and CMK access logging.
- Audit: configure audit logs to push to their Splunk instance and show immutable retention controls (at least 2 years, longer for certain logs).
- Data residency: ensure all storage and logs remain in eu-west-1 region; provide documentation of data flows.
- Integration tests: run end-to-end synthetic chat and embedding workloads, measure p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Security review: deliver security checklist and answer SOC2/ISO questions; provide architecture diagram for their Infosec team.

Acceptance criteria for sign-off:
- Successful Terraform/Helm deployment in their VPC (no changes required to their default egress rules beyond documented exceptions).
- KMS integration validated: customer-managed CMK used for datastore + KV cache encryption; audit logs show key usage events.
- Performance: p95 latency < 210ms (temporary tolerance) for chat baseline test; embeddings throughput >= 40 rps sustained during 30-minute run.
- Audit logging: logs delivered to Splunk and visible to customer security team; retention policy demonstrated.
- Compliance docs: SOC2 mapping doc + answers to top 20 Infosec questions submitted.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-02-10: Intro call (Hannah O.) — outlined requirements, high-level feasibility: positive.
- 2026-02-18: Technical scoping session (Marco R.) — agreed POC scope, shared preliminary Terraform module. (fireflies ff_20260218_LOD-POC-01)
- 2026-02-25: Security review kickoff with Lodestar Infosec; they sent baseline questionnaire.
- 2026-03-02: Follow-up call with KMS SME; customer requested HSM options. (fireflies ff_20260302_Infosec-QA)
- 2026-03-05: Received approval from cloud ops to provision infra outside maintenance window; scheduled POC for week of 2026-03-22.

Action items / Next steps (short):
- Provide final Terraform variables and example IAM policies for cross-account KMS roles (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Prepare perf harness scripts and synthetic prompts (owner: Performance eng).
- Share SOC2 mapping + architecture diagram (owner: Hannah Ortega).
- Legal to provide data residency appendix draft (owner: Redwood legal).

Notes on risks / mitigation:
- Risk: KMS cross-account role delays stall POC. Mitigation: pre-create role templates and use delegated admin flow as fallback.
- Risk: Splunk ingestion throttling; Mitigation: batch logs and use S3+forwarder if needed.

Customer sentiment: cautious but pragmatic — values predictable economics and a clear path to full private deployment. Good fit for Redwood's Private + Optimize features.
